sentences.text:
1 order dated 04-5-2001 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First 2 apeal715.03 Class, Mul convicting the respondent-accused for offence punishable under Section 16(i)(a)(ii) read with Section 7(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act ("Act" for short) is set aside and the accused is acquitted.
2. Heard Shri S.S. Doifode, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State and Shri M.P.
Khajanchi, learned Counsel for the accused.
3. The prosecution case :
Food Inspector, Chandrapur Shri A.S. Dhule accompanied by panch Kisan Shende visited the grocery shop of the accused at village Rajoli, Tahsil - Mul at 12-15 p.m. on 19-1-1994.
Shri A.S. Dhule disclosed his identity and conveyed that he wished to take sample of groundnut oil and gram dal for the purpose of analysis.
Shri A.S. Dhule purchased 450 gram groundnut oil from a packed tin of 15 kg. in the presence of the panch.
He also purchased 750 gram dal.
Notice in form 14-A was given to the accused and an acknowledgment obtained.
The groundnut oil was divided in three equal parts and each part was poured in separate clean glass bottles.
Each bottle was sealed with cork and wrapped in thick paper.

One part of the sample was sent 3 apeal715.03 to the Public Analysis, Pune who submitted report dated 22-2-1994 to the effect that the sample did not confer to the standards prescribed in the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.
The chana dal which was purchased from the shop was also divided in three equal parts and poured in three clean dry empty plastic containers which were sealed by lead.
The sample label was signed by the Food Inspector, the panch witness Kisan Shende and the accused.
One part of the sample was analyzed and the report dated 22-2-194 opines that the sample did not confirm to the standard of chana dal as per the Rules.
The case of the prosecution is that vide letter dated 04-4-1994 submitted to the Food Inspector Shri Ghule, the accused disclosed that he did not purchase Deepak Brand Groundnut Oil.
The Food Inspector obtained the statutory sanction of the Act and filed a complaint on 29-6-1995.

4. The learned Magistrate convicted the accused for offence punishable under Section 16(i)(a)(ii)
read with Section 7(i) of the Act and sentenced him to suffer simple imprisonment for six months and to payment of fine of Rs.2,000/- which judgment is upset by the appellate Court.
I have scrutinized the record in the light of the submissions advanced by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor Shri S.S. Doifode and the learned Counsel Shri M.P Khajanchi for the accused.
I have considered the reasons given by the learned Sessions Judge for acquitting the accused.
6. The learned Sessions Judge has recorded a finding that the notice dated 01-7-1995 issued to the accused intimating that the complaint is instituted on 29-6-1995 is defective.
The said finding is State Of Mah.

sentences.text: I have perused the record of the trial Court.
The assumption of the learned Sessions Judge is factually incorrect.

The notice clearly states that the complaint is instituted in the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Mul and is assigned number 48/95.
7.

entities.text: Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Mul
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned Sessions Judge has further recorded a finding that Rule 14 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules is contravened.
There is no evidence on record to indicate that before taking the sample in the bottles, the Food Inspector had cleaned and dried the bottles.
The evidence of the Food Inspector is examined by 5 apeal715.03 the learned Sessions Judge with extra caution since the only independent witness P.W.5 Kisan Shende did not support the prosecution.
Several circumstances are noted by the learned Sessions Judge to hold that Rule 14 was not complied with scrupulously.
Concededly, the sample was obtained from a sealed and packed tin of groundnut oil.
The sample was not directly drawn in glass bottles.

According to P.W.1 Shri Dhule, the accused sold him 450 gram groundnut oil of Deepak Brand in a clean and dry and empty stainless Steel utensil,
which was supplied by the accused.
P.W.1 states that after showing the utensil to the panch and the accused the groundnut oil was poured in the utensil.
However, that accused supplied a dry and cleaned steel utensil at the request of P.W.1 is not specifically mentioned in panchanama (Exhibit 63).

The evidence of the Food Inspector does not suggest that utensil in which the oil was poured before the samples were poured in the glass bottles was cleaned by either the Food Inspector or any other person.

The learned Sessions Judge has after holistically appreciating the evidence on record and taking note of the fact that the panch witness P.W.5 did not support the prosecution, held that the prosecution did not prove due compliance of mandatory provisions of Rule 14.
In this view of the matter, the learned Sessions Judge extended the benefit of the doubt to the 6 apeal715.03 accused.
8. Shri M.P. Khajanchi would submit, that there is no evidence on record to suggest that the sample collected was of representative character in the absence of evidence that the oil was stirred.
This submission is well merited.
9. The view taken by the learned Sessions Judge is a possible view.
The acquittal only strengthens the presumption of innocence.
The learned Additional Public Prosecutor did not bring to my notice any perversity of approach or in appreciation of evidence to warrant interference in the judgment and order of acquittal.
10. The appeal is sans merit and is rejected.
JUDGE adgokar State Of Mah.
